findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Justify S6 transition-replay's novelty against the established map-or-drift approach it already ships as its fallback: state the concrete failure map-or-drift leaves unaddressed (a scenario where replaying recorded intermediate hops materially improves the outcome over drifting the terminal status), so the added path clears the Rule-of-Three / anti-repackaging bar.
evidence: Plan: 'S6 adds new dispatcher logic that derives the intended local hop sequence from the ticket's core STATUS event log ... re-attempts each intermediate hop ... aborting to drift on the first hop the target rejects'

Retrieved web prior art (Getint, Exalate, TFS4JIRA, Jira Align docs) shows tracker-sync tools resolve workflow-transition variance via status MAPPING and drift, not by replaying an intermediate hop trail — so replay is a novel addition not reflected in established tools

ABSENCE: the plan asserts replay is 'new code' and bounds it, but never states what concrete failure map-or-drift leaves unaddressed that warrants the extra replay path (Rule-of-Three / anti-repackaging)
findings.finding: S6's transition-replay mechanism is a novel departure from the established map-or-drift approach for non-allowed transitions (the norm in commercial trackers-sync tools, and the fallback S6 itself already ships), but the plan does not justify replay's added complexity against that simpler established alternative.
findings.location: Approach section (transition replay) + Child S6 + AC line 'A non-allowed transition is attempted by replay...'
scenarios: A reviewer or maintainer questioning whether the replay path earns its complexity vs. simply mapping/drifting the terminal status
A future backend adapter author deciding whether replay is core-neutral behavior worth reusing or Jira-workflow-specific gold-plating
findings.suggested_fix: Add a short rationale to S6 (and the Approach paragraph) giving a concrete scenario where replaying the recorded hop trail produces a correct target state that a single map-to-terminal-status could not — e.g. a target workflow that gates the final status behind an intermediate transition side effect — and note why that scenario is common enough in real project workflows to justify the mechanism over pure drift.
